author: barnabasbusa
content: hey, I'm just getting back from holiday, so might have missed some discussion about why we need `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` at all. Shouldn't blob retention be a function of some epochs? Why would we ever wanna keep it 18d if we can get away with less time, due to shorter slots?

author: barnabasbusa
content: I assume rollups might be hardcoding time not epochs?

author: barnabemonnot
content:
The reason it was set to 18d afaik was to accommodate for optimistic rollups using 7 day challenge windows. In the worst case, an adversary and a challenger can each use up to 7 days for their answers in a dispute, i.e., a max dispute time of 14d. I believe 18d was chosen because smallest power of 2 (4096 epochs) that is greater than 14d.

So it's not that "we can get away with less time", if that time is a wall-clock constraint more than an epoch-based one.

author: barnabasbusa
content: ok. I was under the assumptions that rollups used epochs not seconds for their challenge windows.

author: barnabasbusa
content: But I guess the challange window is more human focused not machine focused, so we wanna keep it actually 7d even if we have shorter slots.

author: barnabemonnot
content: Actually recently L2Beat communicated that 5 days window was good enough for optimistic rollups, and there were active discussions to socially coordinate around an even lower number

author: barnabemonnot
content: I would be personally fine with reducing the blob retention window, but this should be a more intentional decision imo, not happen as a side effect of shortening slot (where the principle is to try and keep every invariant as much as we can)
